f.title: Characterise short-term ADE rates (about 1% cumulative 3-month incidence) during clinical development
f.statement: It is expected that short-term adverse event rates (cumulative 3-month incidence of about 1%) will be well characterised during clinical development. Events whose rate of occurrence changes over a longer period may need to be characterised depending on their severity and importance to the risk-benefit assessment. The safety evaluation during clinical development is not expected to characterise rare adverse events, for example those occurring in fewer than 1 in 1000 patients.
f.topic: Extent of exposure for safety database
f.applicability: Drugs intended for long-term treatment (chronic or repeated intermittent use for longer than 6 months) of non-life-threatening conditions
f.exceptions: Rare adverse events (e.g. fewer than 1 in 1000 patients) are not expected to be characterised.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.title: Treat enough patients for 6 months at clinical doses to characterise the pattern of ADEs over time
f.statement: The number of patients treated for 6 months at dosage levels intended for clinical use should be adequate to characterise the pattern of adverse drug events (ADEs) over time. To achieve this, the cohort of exposed subjects should be large enough to observe whether more frequently occurring events increase or decrease over time and to observe delayed events of reasonable frequency (e.g., in the general range of 0.5%-5%). Usually 300-600 patients should be adequate.
f.topic: Extent of exposure for safety database
f.applicability: Drugs intended for long-term treatment (chronic or repeated intermittent use for longer than 6 months) of non-life-threatening conditions
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.title: Include about 100 patients with at least one-year exposure from prospective studies at clinical doses
f.statement: 100 patients exposed for a minimum of one year is considered acceptable to include as part of the safety database. The data should come from prospective studies appropriately designed to provide at least one year of exposure at dosage levels intended for clinical use.
f.topic: Extent of exposure for safety database
f.applicability: Drugs intended for long-term treatment (chronic or repeated intermittent use for longer than 6 months) of non-life-threatening conditions

f.title: Plan for a total safety database of about 1500 treated individuals
f.statement: It is anticipated that the total number of individuals treated with the investigational drug, including short-term exposure, will be about 1500. Japan currently accepts 500-1500 patients; the potential for a smaller number is due to Japan's post-marketing surveillance requirement, with the actual number for a specific drug determined by the information available on the drug and drug class.

f.applicability: Drugs intended for long-term treatment (chronic or repeated intermittent use for longer than 6 months) of non-life-threatening conditions

f.title: Expect a larger and/or longer-term safety database where late-developing or worsening ADEs are a concern
f.statement: Instances where there is concern that the drug will cause late-developing ADEs, or ADEs that increase in severity or frequency over time, would require a larger and/or longer-term safety database. The concern could arise from data from animal studies; clinical information from other agents with related chemical structures or from a related pharmacologic class; or pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic properties known to be associated with such ADEs.
f.topic: Extent of exposure for safety database
f.applicability: Drugs intended for long-term treatment (chronic or repeated intermittent use for longer than 6 months) of non-life-threatening conditions
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.title: Expect a greater long-term database to quantify an expected specific low-frequency ADE
f.statement: Situations in which there is a need to quantitate the occurrence rate of an expected specific low-frequency ADE will require a greater long-term database, for example where a specific serious ADE has been identified in similar drugs or where a serious event that could represent an alert event is observed in early clinical trials.

f.title: Consider larger safety databases where the benefit is small, limited to a fraction of patients or uncertain
f.statement: Larger safety databases may be needed to make risk/benefit decisions where the benefit from the drug is small, will be experienced by only a fraction of the treated patients, or is of uncertain magnitude (e.g., efficacy determined on a surrogate endpoint).
f.topic: Extent of exposure for safety database

rows.quote: Larger safety data bases may be needed to make risk/benefit decisions in situations where the benefit from the drug is either (1) small (e.g., symptomatic improvement in less serious medical conditions) or (2) will be experienced by only a fraction of the treated patients (e.g., certain preventive therapies administered to healthy populations) or (3) is of uncertain magnitude (e.g., efficacy determination on a surrogate endpoint).

f.title: Power trials to detect increases over background morbidity or mortality where relevant
f.statement: Where there is concern that a drug may add to an already significant background rate of morbidity or mortality, clinical trials may need to be designed with a sufficient number of patients to provide adequate statistical power to detect prespecified increases over the baseline morbidity or mortality.
